title: Global value chain participation and innovation: firm-level evidence from Africa
summary: The paper asks whether engagement in global value chains (GVCs) is linked to the innovative capabilities of firms in Africa.
keyFindings: Firms in Africa that engage in GVC activities are more likely to introduce innovative products onto markets.
The result holds after addressing reverse causality, and is robust to alternative definitions of GVC and innovation and to a different identification strategy.
methods: World Bank Enterprise Survey firm-level data.
